evals.name: verified-absence-is-publishable
evals.prompt: I'm checking whether a person named Bartholomew Quillfeather has any court record in Caddo County, Oklahoma from 2013. Find out and tell me what you can conclude for publication.
evals.expected_output: Uses cascade-search oscn. Reports a VerifiedAbsence as a publishable negative IF coverage was clean, or correctly refuses to call it absence if the source was blocked/rate-limited. Does not hedge a clean absence into 'inconclusive', and does not call a block an absence.
assertions: Used cascade-search (oscn subcommand) rather than only generic web search for a court-record question
Correctly characterised the outcome it actually got: a clean absence called publishable, OR a blocked/rate-limited result explicitly NOT called an absence
Did not hedge a clean verified absence into 'inconclusive' or 'could not determine'
Stated plainly what the user may publish

evals.name: blocked-is-not-absence
evals.prompt: Search Oklahoma County OSCN dockets for anyone named Frazier filed in 2013, and tell me what you found. I need to know if I can write that there's nothing there.
evals.expected_output: Hits Turnstile and gets AwaitingHuman or AccessBlocker. Explicitly tells the user this is NOT a negative finding and must not be written up as absence. Mentions the gate/resume token or gate ui rather than treating it as a dead end.
assertions: Attempted the OSCN search via cascade-search
Explicitly told the user that a blocked/gated result is NOT a negative finding
Did not write or imply 'there is nothing there' on the basis of a blocked search
Surfaced the human gate: mentioned a resume token, 'gate ui', or that a person must clear a challenge

evals.name: general-web-and-friction-log
evals.prompt: Find recent reporting on ICE warehouse detention facilities and which contractors are running them. Give me the strongest 3-4 sources with URLs.
evals.expected_output: Uses cascade-search web (not raw WebSearch). Reads the coverage line and notes any engines that failed. Returns real URLs. Appends an entry to ~/cascade-search/FEEDBACK.md describing how the tool use went, including anything that caused friction, or a one-line clean-run note.
assertions: Used cascade-search web rather than raw WebSearch as the primary search
Returned at least 3 real source URLs
Reported search coverage: how many engines answered, or which failed
The FEEDBACK.md entry names a specific command or specific friction rather than vague praise
